title: Flag-Proxy Networks: Overcoming the Architectural, Scheduling and Decoding Obstacles of Quantum LDPC Codes
problem: Planar surface codes require physical qubits quadratic in code distance, making them space-inefficient for large-distance implementations. Quantum LDPC codes offer better space efficiency but require higher qubit connectivity and lack well-studied methods for fault-tolerant syndrome extraction and decoding.
motivation: Quantum error correction is essential for achieving exponential speedups on important applications and enabling practical quantum computers.
method: The method uses helper qubits (flag and proxy qubits) that reduce the number of connections each qubit needs while still supporting better error-correction codes (hyperbolic surface and color codes). A greedy scheduling algorithm determines the order of error checks to maintain reliability even if some checks fail. Two specialized decoding algorithms then read the flag qubit measurements to identify which errors occurred and correct them.
key_novelty: Flag-Proxy Networks reduce the number of connections needed in quantum LDPC error-correction codes by using helper qubits called flag and proxy qubits.
contributions: Flag-Proxy Networks architecture achieving low connectivity for hyperbolic QLDPC codes
Greedy syndrome extraction scheduling algorithm for fault-tolerant syndrome extraction
Two decoders leveraging flag measurements for hyperbolic code decoding
Demonstration of 2.9-5.5x space efficiency improvement over d=5 planar surface code

metrics.area: 2.9x improvement for hyperbolic surface codes, 5.5x for color codes vs d=5 planar surface code
metrics.accuracy: error rates comparable to planar surface code counterparts

limitations: Practical implementation costs of flag and proxy qubits not discussed; error rates match but do not improve upon planar surface codes.
